action: If Accuver or LIG Accuver is a supplier or partner, ask them directly for confirmation before acting; watch for phishing that uses the claim.
date_note: Date of the leak-site post as reported by Daily SECU citing Brandefense; Cyber Insights logged it at 21:35 UTC that day, which the article calls its detection time.
exec: Unverified extortion claim; relevant if Accuver or LIG Accuver is a supplier or customer.
place: South Korea (city not stated; unclear which Accuver entity is meant)
plain: A ransomware group lists Accuver on its leak site. The company has not confirmed anything, and no intrusion or leak has been verified.
summary: Daily SECU reports that the Everest ransomware group listed Accuver (accuver.com), the overseas brand of LIG Accuver, as a victim on 20 November, citing Brandefense. The article says no independent evidence of intrusion or data theft has been found, and gives no data volume. It reports no statement from the company.
title: Everest lists Accuver, overseas brand of LIG Accuver, on its leak site

validation.note: Single publisher (Daily SECU, relaying Brandefense and trackers); leak-site claim, no statement from the company in the article.

review.note: Compared title, 20 Nov post date (Brandefense), claimed status/severity 1, no company statement, no evidence of intrusion or data volume against Daily SECU article (21 Nov); single publisher so unconfirmed_claim is right
